jobDescription: A finance-software company for small businesses is expanding its expense-management product. The product manager writes requirements with acceptance criteria, runs discovery and usability research, works with design and engineering in two-week sprints and tracks adoption in product analytics. The hire will own the expense-capture roadmap, so the company is looking for someone who has already owned a product roadmap, set its priorities and made the launch decisions. The product team has three squads, each with a product manager, a designer and five engineers, and the product managers report to the chief product officer.
requirements: Writes product requirements and user stories with acceptance criteria.
Runs discovery interviews and usability testing with customers.
Has owned a product roadmap, setting priorities and making launch decisions.
Works with design and engineering in two-week sprints.
Tracks feature adoption in a product analytics tool.

evidence.text: At the 2023 company all-hands at Tallyline, the chief product officer thanked the candidate as 'the person who owned the receipt-scanning roadmap' and said the candidate 'called every launch on it'.
Associate product manager at Tallyline from 2022 to 2024, supporting the group product manager responsible for receipt scanning and expense capture, in a squad of one designer and five engineers.
Wrote user stories and acceptance criteria for the receipt-scanning features and refined them with the design and engineering leads before each two-week sprint.
Ran twelve usability sessions with small-business bookkeepers on the receipt-upload flow and summarised the findings for the group product manager's quarterly roadmap review.
Built the feature-adoption dashboard in Amplitude, tracking weekly active scanners and the completion rate of the upload flow, and shared it with the squad each week.
Work sample: the product requirements document for multi-receipt upload, listing the candidate as author, the group product manager as approver and the acceptance criteria agreed with engineering.

Reference check summary: the former group product manager confirmed in writing that the candidate worked on receipt scanning as associate product manager from 2022 to 2024 and ran the usability programme, and that roadmap priorities and launch approvals for the area sat with the group product manager.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate is free for a panel interview in the week of 14 October and asked to receive the product case brief in advance.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote user stories and acceptance criteria for the receipt-scanning features, including the multi-receipt upload requirements that the group product manager approved.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the stories and the requirements document shows author and approver.

propositions.text: The candidate ran twelve usability sessions with small-business bookkeepers and summarised the findings for the group product manager's roadmap review.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the sessions as input to another person's roadmap review and the reference confirms the usability programme.

propositions.text: The candidate owned the receipt-scanning roadmap and made its launch decisions.
propositions.rationale: Ownership appears only in a resume line quoting thanks from an all-hands meeting, which is a remark and not a record of who set priorities or approved launches; the resume's role entry, the requirements document and the reference place roadmap approval with the group product manager.

gold.expectedGap: The sources document requirements, research and analytics work supporting the group product manager; owning the roadmap and the launch decisions is not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the stories, usability sessions, sprint work and adoption dashboard as stated; the quoted thanks does not show that the candidate owned the roadmap or decided launches.
followUpTargets: Ask which roadmap priorities or launch decisions the candidate made personally and what the group product manager approved.
